summary: Across 4, 80, 150 and 300 K the monolayer CrSBr spectrum is dominated by one mode near 341 cm-1, which is stable from 4 to 80 K and then softens with a normal anharmonic-looking trend. The changes that matter are in the weaker bands: a band at ~358 cm-1 appears only below ~150 K (between 80 and 150 K, which brackets bulk T_N ~132 K), a broad band at ~300 cm-1 is present to at least 150 K but not clearly at 300 K, and the ~240 cm-1 mode softens by ~2 cm-1 between 80 and 150 K, about three times the shift of the 341 mode over the same interval. These are suggestive of magnetic-order-related effects, but with four temperatures, uncalibrated absolute intensities and no polarization series, I can't separate them from calibration drift, laser heating or ordinary anharmonicity. The most important caveat is that absolute intensities differ by factors of 2.6-3.8 between 4 and 80 K for every mode, so only within-spectrum ratios and positions can be compared.

observations.finding: Dominant mode at ~341 cm-1: centre and width stay flat from 4 to 80 K (341.41 vs 341.32 cm-1; FWHM 5.1 vs 5.2 cm-1), then soften to 340.58 cm-1 at 150 K and 338.38 cm-1 at 300 K (FWHM 6.9 cm-1). This is consistent with ordinary anharmonic behaviour; no anomaly can be resolved in this mode from four temperatures.

The ~240 cm-1 mode softens by ~2.1 cm-1 between 80 and 150 K, about three times the shift of the 341 mode over the same interval, so it is the only mode whose shift is out of step with the 341 mode in this set. It is a candidate for spin-phonon coupling near T_N, but four temperatures cannot distinguish a kink from anharmonicity, and the calibration drift is of the same size.
observations.evidence: Centres: 4 K 242.06±0.27, 80 K 242.11±0.37, 150 K 239.96±0.34, 300 K 237.02±0.25 cm-1. Shift 80->150 K: -2.15±0.50 cm-1 (240 mode) vs -0.74±0.14 cm-1 (341 mode). Shift 150->300 K: -2.9 vs -2.2 cm-1. Peak is significant at all T (drop-peak dBIC +97 to +155). FWHM 7.3, 10.8, 8.9, 9.8 cm-1 is non-monotonic and not reliable.

observations.finding: A narrow band at ~358 cm-1 is present at 4 K (height 65, area ~713, centre 358.36±0.33) and 80 K (height 17, centre 357.7±0.6) and is not significant at 150 K (dBIC -11 when dropped) or 300 K. Its emergence between 80 and 150 K brackets the bulk T_N (~132 K).
observations.evidence: Drop-band dBIC: 4 K +89, 80 K +40, 150 K -11, 300 K -14. Area ratio 358/341: 0.39 at 4 K, 0.40 at 80 K. The 150 K fit gives height 6.4±5.4, i.e. consistent with zero.

observations.finding: A broad band at ~300 cm-1 (centre 299-300 cm-1) is significant at 4, 80 and 150 K but not at 300 K. Its width decreases with increasing temperature (FWHM 20.3, 15.0, 12.1 cm-1 at 4, 80, 150 K), which is opposite to the usual phonon behaviour. That suggests a composite band, a non-phonon contribution, or fit degeneracy with the 341 wing.
observations.evidence: Height 39.3 (4 K), 14.4 (80 K), 17.5 (150 K). Drop-band dBIC +81, +48, +48 at 4, 80, 150 K. At 300 K dBIC -5 and the fitted centre is unphysical (292 cm-1). The 300 K noise is 6.7 counts, so the upper limit on height is roughly 20 counts, comparable to the 150 K amplitude; absence at 300 K is not established. At 4 K, the residuals are structured at 308 cm-1 (+8 counts) and 315-320 cm-1 (-6 counts), and adding a second band in this region does not improve BIC.

observations.finding: Absolute intensities are not comparable between temperatures. Between 4 and 80 K all bands drop by similar factors, so the 4 K trace is brighter for reasons that are not mode-specific. Mode-to-mode height ratios are roughly constant between 4 and 80 K, which argues for a global scaling (laser power, integration time, collection or heating) rather than a change in the material.
observations.evidence: 4 K/80 K height ratios: 341 cm-1 3.1, 240 cm-1 2.6, 301 cm-1 2.7, 358 cm-1 3.8. Height ratios 301/341: 0.17 (4 K), 0.20 (80 K), 0.16 (150 K). Height ratios 240/341: 0.34 (4 K), 0.42 (80 K). Peak-free noise (160-220 and 370-400 cm-1): 5.9 (4 K), 2.7 (80 K), 3.3 (150 K), 6.7 (300 K), so the acquisition conditions evidently differ between traces.

observations.finding: Missing points sit at fixed shift positions across the traces, which suggests detector-pixel masking or cosmic-ray removal rather than a sample feature. Gaps are at 328.1-330.7 cm-1 in all traces (328.1-332.0 at 80 K), 167.2-169.8 at 80 K, and 362.0-364.6 and 369.7-372.3 at 4 K. The 328-332 gap lies on the low-energy flank of the 341 cm-1 mode and coincides with a residual bump at 332-336 cm-1 at 4 K. Points were not interpolated.
observations.evidence: Grid step 1.314 cm-1, n=188/188/190/191 points at 4/80/150/300 K, no NaN values; gaps identified as steps > 1.5x median.

observations.finding: Negative intensities after background subtraction (to -18 counts at 300 K near 160-175 cm-1 and -12 at 4 K) indicate imperfect background subtraction; the 300 K baseline is the worst.
observations.evidence: Minimum intensity: 4 K -11.6, 80 K -8.2, 150 K -6.4, 300 K -18.4. The 300 K negative excursion between 160 and 180 cm-1 is systematic, not single-pixel noise.

observations.finding: Within the 150-400 cm-1 window the spectrum shows no feature that clearly indicates strong defects or strain; the 341 cm-1 mode is narrow (~5 cm-1 FWHM at 4 K), which is consistent with good crystal quality. Interpretation of defect level rests on this single width and on the absence of other bands here, not on a reference.
observations.evidence: 341 cm-1 FWHM 5.07 cm-1 at 4 K with an instrument response that is unknown (grating/slit not given).

observations.finding: A monolayer CrSBr has intralayer ferromagnetic order, so an interlayer-antiferromagnetic doubled cell that could fold phonons (the usual explanation for new bands in bulk) does not apply. Any new low-temperature band in the monolayer must therefore be explained by spin-phonon coupling or a change in the magnetic point symmetry, not by zone folding.

caveats: Absolute intensities differ by 2.6-3.8x between 4 K and 80 K for every mode, and 80 K is non-monotonic relative to 4 K and 150 K. Compare only within-spectrum ratios and positions unless acquisition power, integration time and a reference are provided.
Laser heating: the stage temperature is not the sample temperature under 532 nm excitation in vacuum. Power-dependent spectra are needed to rule out heating shifting the low-T points.

Spectrometer calibration: a 2 cm-1 shift of the 240 cm-1 mode between 80 and 150 K is about the size of plausible calibration drift between cooldowns. No reference line (Ne lamp or a standard phonon) is included in the folder.
Spectral resolution is unknown. Mode widths of 5-10 cm-1 can be partly instrumental, so width trends are weak evidence.

Polarization: crossed circular (sigma+ in / sigma- out) in backscatter selects a subset of modes that depends on the symmetry and convention. No linear or angle-resolved data are provided, so no mode symmetry can be assigned from these spectra.

The ~358 and ~301 cm-1 bands are weak (height/noise ~5-7 at 4-80 K). The 150 K and 300 K non-detections are upper limits set by noise, not proof of absence: the 300 K noise is 6.7 counts, twice the 150 K noise.
4 K residuals are structured near 300-340 cm-1 (reduced chi-square 71). The 301 band's width and centre at 4 K are therefore model-dependent.
Window starts at 151 cm-1: low-frequency modes and the notch/edge-filter region are not covered, and an edge-filter roll-off could affect the first ~20 cm-1.
Monolayer intralayer ferromagnetism means the bulk-style zone-folding argument for new bands does not apply (see observations).
Only four temperatures; T_N cannot be located from them. A dense sweep (about 10 K steps between 100 and 160 K) is needed to test for a kink.
questions_for_user: What were the laser power at the sample, integration time, grating/slit and number of accumulations for each trace? Without these, the absolute intensity differences (4 K brighter than 80 K by ~3x for every mode) cannot be interpreted.
Was the spectrometer calibrated (Ne lamp or a standard phonon) at each cooldown? A 2 cm-1 shift of the 240 cm-1 mode between 80 and 150 K is at the level of possible calibration drift.
Was the background subtraction done by a measured dark/background spectrum or a fitted baseline? The 300 K trace has systematic negative values (to -18 counts).
Were the missing points at 328-332 cm-1 (all traces) and 167-170, 362-365, 370-372 cm-1 caused by detector-pixel masking or cosmic-ray removal? The 328-332 gap sits on the 341 cm-1 flank.
Did you measure power dependence and linear or angle-resolved polarization? These would test laser heating and give mode symmetries that the single crossed-circular configuration cannot.
Is there a reference spectrum of bulk or few-layer CrSBr taken with the same setup? Monolayer-specific bands are easier to identify with a bulk reference.
What is the independent T_N of this monolayer (magneto-optical, SHG, or magnetotransport)? The 358 cm-1 onset is only bracketed between 80 and 150 K.
Was the sample encapsulated (for example in hBN) or exposed to air between exfoliation and measurement? Degradation could change the band structure near 240-360 cm-1.
